answer: Each earning key is bound to one terraced plot in a walled garden below a surveyed summit hut. The registrar issues an unpublished fable, recited live on the plot's datum stone into a wind-sheltered horn. The spectrogram, survey pin, and soil-core hash become the only credential that can later post a harvest. To be paid the grower must return, tend a marked lot, and match that recital as inspectors check the core. A valley replay or a second body on the same terrace fails. N sybils require N summit plots and N gardens, a cost that scales with scarce high land, not cheap keypairs.
